stages.name: Dock in the water
stages.text: Water in the tank and gel in both parts from the first frame. The tail slides forward and docks from behind, its gel face against the gel face of the head; the last 10 mm slowly. Nine magnets in the tail face pull the steel disks in the cuff of the quilted head.

stages.name: Unfold, top up
stages.text: The arm unfolds. The gel is already in (4.79 L); the line on the arm only tops up the 42 mL that left with the last newborn.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The electromagnet picks the electronics kit once, from its place in the tail, and carries the kit through the gel to the print seat, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change in the tail: holder off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release). The needle travels in the gel to the print.

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the next head folded flat around its kit: 626 m of bead, 1.17 L of Dragon Skin 30.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, holder on.

stages.name: Birth: failed check
stages.text: The birth through the mouth is not shown: every way tried failed (Birth tab).

notes: The tank is full and the gel is in from the start: each part holds its own gel at the open docking face, level with the water. The tail slides forward along the floor and docks from behind; the two gel faces meet and the water between them is squeezed out. Nine magnets in the tail face pull the steel disks in the cuff of the quilted head; the cuff seals on the cord seat.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, over the gel. The base does not move.
The line on the arm tops up the gel that left with the last newborn (42 mL); no filling, the gel stays from birth to birth.
The bare arm folds back into the tail.
The bare arm turns to the holder: an electromagnet and a ball needle on a saddle beside the arm.
The quick release slides onto the holder and clicks.
The holder leaves its saddle sideways, its needle in the gel, and turns to the kit, which waits in the gel in front of the arm.
The magnet lands on the steel disk of the kit.
Magnet on: the magnet holds the kit by the steel disk.
The kit is carried forward through the gel, across the seam, to the print seat.
The kit goes down onto the three seat bumps.
Magnet off: the kit stays on the seat, held by the gel; the holder lifts clear.
Tool change in the tail: the holder comes back through the gel.
The holder slides sideways onto its saddle.
The pin on the saddle presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm turns to the print needle on the other side.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle leaves its saddle sideways, its tip in the gel.
The needle moves forward through the gel, across the seam, to the print.
The next head is printed folded flat, 18 layers, around its kit, layer by layer, in Dragon Skin 30.
The silicone cures in the gel (Dragon Skin 30: 16 hours at room temperature, Smooth-On bulletin). The print needle goes back over the print to its saddle in the tail.
The holder is back on the arm: the ball needle beside the magnet now carries the air.
Birth: the holder moves toward the mouth over the folded next head.
This is as far as the holder reaches: x = 271 mm. The lower lip is at x = 366 mm, 95 mm further.

Failed check, no birth is shown: the folded head does not pass the mouth as a block, a strip that does pass does not fit the print room, and at the height of the lip the last 92 mm before it are beyond the reach of the arm. See the Birth tab.

checks.name: Tail in two prints, each one piece on the H2S: front (docking face, arm, saddles, kit magazine) 247 x 314 x 336 mm, rear (the store and the taper, with the sleeve of the joint) 230 x 220 x 316 mm, of 340 x 320 x 340
Everything for the tools is behind the docking plane: the saddles, the two modules and the kit store end 4 mm behind the plane. Only the stems and the kit stand in the gel, which runs across the seam

No tool crosses a wall: close to its base the arm holds the needle tip at most 18 mm high (at 150 mm from the axis), so the print needle and the holder hang with their stems in the gel and travel in the gel to the print; a wall at the docking plane could be only 17 mm tall
Folded arm ends 50 mm behind the docking plane; tower top 11 mm under the tail roof
The print needle reaches all 925 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges
The next head leaves through the mouth, over the lower lip, without clipping
checks.value: failed: no way found, see the Birth tab; not shown on the timeline

checks.name: Tried: Push the pack as one block, as the doublewall build pushed its flat pack. The pack (123 x 194 x 79 mm) does not pass the mouth as a block (48 mm short of the opening at its tightest height). Even narrower, it would have to leave the gel and climb onto the lower lip, which stands 4.5 mm above the gel and 26.4 mm above the water: on the lip the whole newborn (1.57 kg) is in air, 15.4 N against the DexArm payload of 4.9 N, and the friction alone (0.3) is 4.6 N. And at the height of the lip the holder reaches x = 274 mm, so the rear of the pack stays 92 mm inside the mouth.

Tried: Unfold the pack in the gel and feed the strip out flat over the lip, the arm pushing hand over hand at bosses; the last part freed by the parent body backing away. A flat strip folded 7 across (83 mm wide, 62 mm thick) is the least folded strip that passes the mouth on the lip (8 mm to spare; folded 6 across it would clear the rim by only 0.7 mm, under the 2 mm kept). Pushed flat over the lip it does not buckle, and the push is about 1.6 N (friction on the lip in air 1.0 N, gel drag 0.5 N at 25 Pa), under the payload. The last 92 mm beyond the reach of the holder could come from the parent body backing away on the drive of the relay while the opened part outside rests on the floor (anchor about 2.6 N). But that strip does not fit the print room: folded 2 along the pack is 175 mm long where the needle serves 93 mm; folded 3 along it stands 185 mm tall where the gel allows 93 mm. With 1.0 mm skins and 0.8 mm gaps it would still be 175 mm long (2 along) or 151 mm tall (3 along).

Tried: Push the strip partly inflated, so that it carries the push like a beam and can be pushed past the reach. Inflated, each of the 14 layers of the strip folded 7 across is 17 mm deep (median cell): the strip becomes 250 mm thick and 83 mm wide, 76 mm more than the mouth gives at the heights it must pass. Inflating only some layers leaves the others to buckle. And the interlayer air does not drive the body forward: it fills cells, it does not lengthen the body, and the trailing rim is the widest section of the newborn, so the last 92 mm still stay beyond the reach.

Reach: the holder (ball needle, official joint ranges) reaches x = 274 mm at the height of the lip shelf (110 mm), 284 mm at most lower down, where the chin of the head is in the way; the lower lip is at x = 366 mm, 92 mm further

The gel has its place: the lower part of the head (the lobe, now 224 mm wide, simple version 96) holds 4.79 L with the folded next head in (simple version 2.85 L); the gel stands at 100 mm, 4.5 mm under the lip

Water level with the gel without the print: 78.7 mm (simple version 88.5 mm). With the print in, the gel stands 21 mm higher than the water, 216 Pa at the floor on the soft lobe walls; spanning floor to shelf they use 33 percent of their wrinkling moment (x 2 on the load); as a cantilever from the floor 85 percent

Cells: 364, 14 to 42 mm across (median 21), irregular, their direction turning along the body; smallest at the docking rim, the mouth and the lip, largest on the roof; the lobe walls 24 mm. Six serpentine circuits (lobe, flank and roof, each side), filled from the mouth end; 94 percent of the steps go to a neighboring cell, 23 need a short channel

Dragon Skin 10 NV first: the section above the gel as a two hinged arch on the lobe needs 3.36 kPa (loads x 2), the largest bulge of its cells allows 1.28 kPa (limit point / 1.5). Nine variants of cell size and bulge tried, none passes

Dragon Skin 30: needs 3.36 kPa, allows 4.09 kPa; working pressure 3.73 kPa, margin 1.11 on the need and 1.10 on the allowed value; skins 1.2 mm, webs 0.8 mm; the cells 11 to 34 mm deep, no gel ballast in the cells
checks.value: Dragon Skin 30 printed in Carbopol is a bench test

checks.name: Lower lip, its own weight as a quilted cantilever of 75 mm: 31 percent of its wrinkling moment

Flat pack (laid flat, Z folded 3 across and 3 along, 18 layers of 4.4 mm): 123 x 194 x 79 mm, packing 0.62; the needle serves it from x = 117 mm, 5.7 mm clear of the chin, 15 mm clear of the lobe walls, 17 mm of gel over it
checks.value: 1 mm gel gaps as in the doublewall gates; the simple build kept 2 mm

checks.name: Enlarged lower shell, the form kept: lobe 224 mm wide (simple 96), gel 4.79 L (simple 2.85 L); spindle, roof arc, mouth and lower lip unchanged

Printed full of gel: 0.33 L in the 1 mm gaps. Clearing it inside the parent through a collapsed channel needs 132 kPa (2 tau L / h, 25 Pa, 2.6 m); in the open cells outside, a plug through 4 mm passages 16 to 44 kPa (9 to 25 Pa). Both above the 3.7 kPa of the quilt: the gel stays, as a film and as ballast in the lobe
checks.value: kept, counted as load above the water (0.5 mm film, estimate)

checks.name: Quilted rim on the tail face: nine pairs of DC2-N52 in the face and 18 x 3 mm steel disks in a solid cuff (doublewall gates G4), about 121 N; the air nipple on the face seats in the valve block of the cuff and feeds the six circuits through a relief valve at 3.7 kPa; tilt release 12.8 N per magnet against 39 N of cord (G7)
Tail alone in 78.7 mm of water with its gel, store empty: 10.3 N on the floor; with 1.2 kg of steel under the arm base (allowed for the tail) 20.6 N for the wheels of the relay
Quilted head alone with its gel at the water level: 5.24 kg against 4.83 kg of buoyancy (the air in the lobe cells under the water lifts 0.67 kg): 4.0 N on the floor
Relay and next cycle: not run, because there is no birth
The first head is a quilted head too, cast or printed in a gel bath outside the tank beforehand; the H2S prints only the tail (two prints) and the molds
Per frame penetration test over 1368 frames (arm, tools, kit, the folded next head as it is printed, the inner skin of the head, the rack, the store): deepest overlap of any pair 0.77 mm (limit 1 mm)

verdict.point: Q1 the birth through the mouth, without clipping
verdict.why: Failed after three attempts (Birth tab): the folded head (123 x 194 x 79 mm) does not pass the mouth as a block, and the lip stands 26 mm above the water so the whole newborn (1.57 kg) would weigh in air on it; a strip folded 7 across passes the mouth but does not fit the print room; partly inflated it is too wide. The holder stops 92 mm short of the lip. Not shown on the timeline.

verdict.point: Q2 the gel has its place
verdict.why: The lower part of the head holds 4.79 L at 100 mm; the water stands at the gel level without the print (78.7 mm). The lobe walls are held by their own quilt at 3.7 kPa, the water outside at nearly the same level and the floor; with the print in the gel stands 21 mm over the water (216 Pa), within the walls (estimate).

verdict.ok: yes in Dragon Skin 30, no in 10 NV
verdict.why: 364 cells, 14 to 42 mm, irregular, turning; six serpentine circuits. Dragon Skin 10 NV fails (3.36 kPa needed, 1.28 allowed); Dragon Skin 30 at 3.73 kPa (needs 3.36, allows 4.09).
Flat pack 3 x 3, 123 x 194 x 79 mm, in the enlarged lobe (224 mm wide); every point in the reach of the needle; printed on the timeline.
0.33 L printed in the gaps; clearing needs far more than the quilt pressure inside or outside; it stays as a film and as ballast in the lobe.
Nine magnet pairs and steel disks in the cuff, nipple and relief valve, tilt release, 1.2 kg of steel in the tail. The relay is not run without a birth.

cast outside the tank in a two part mold of the head form (the H2S prints the mold halves and a core for each skin layer), or printed in a gel bath outside beforehand by the same arm on a bench; the H2S prints only the tail (two prints) and the molds.

limits: The birth is the open question: it is shown as a failed check. What would make it possible is listed in the Birth tab; each changes something the brief fixed (the reach of the arm, the form of the mouth, or the open interior during the birth).

The quilt is sized as a 2D two hinged arch per section (loads x 2, the ballooning limit of the largest bulge / 1.5, wrinkling of the skin on the compression side); the shell action along the body is not counted. The cells are drawn with their webs and bulges as computed, the seams as lines.

Bench tests: (1) Dragon Skin 30 printed in Carbopol in 1 mm gaps; (2) a quilted section at 3.7 kPa, crown drop and wrinkling; (3) folding at the seams, 18 layers; (4) the soft lobe walls with the gel 21 mm over the water; (5) gel film left in the cells; (6) the tilt release of the cuff magnets; (7) the open gel face at the water level.
Estimates: the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), friction 0.3, the gel film left in the cells (0.5 mm), the magnet pull through the cuff, the passages between cells (4 mm).
Overlap is measured from sampled points against exact surfaces; the folded next head is tested as its box against the arm and its points against the inner face.

read.tank_text: The tank is the Ultum Nature Systems UNS 150U, 1500 x 600 x 600 mm, 15 mm low iron glass, as in the simple version. The water stands 82 mm deep (the gel level without the print). The relay of this variant would need the wider Glasscages tank of the fertile build (914 mm across); it is not run here, since there is no birth.

With 1.0 mm skins and 0.8 mm gaps it would still be 175 mm long (2 along) or 151 mm tall (3 along).

attempts.name: Push the strip partly inflated, so that it carries the push like a beam and can be pushed past the reach
attempts.why: Inflated, each of the 14 layers of the strip folded 7 across is 17 mm deep (median cell): the strip becomes 250 mm thick and 83 mm wide, 76 mm more than the mouth gives at the heights it must pass. Inflating only some layers leaves the others to buckle. And the interlayer air does not drive the body forward: it fills cells, it does not lengthen the body, and the trailing rim is the widest section of the newborn, so the last 92 mm still stay beyond the reach.

needs: a reach of the holder to about x = 396 mm at the height of the lip (now 274): 122 mm more, for example the DexArm on a slide, which the simple version removed
or a lower lip at the water level and within the reach, which is the shorter head with the mouth open to the floor of the doublewall build, excluded by the brief

or a newborn closed for the birth (thin membranes across the rim and the mouth, cut after the birth), so that its lumen can be inflated and the body grows through the mouth as in the simple version; but the trailing rim is the widest section (1163 mm of perimeter against 665 mm of mouth rim), so it would have to fold in the mouth with nothing to drive it
